Dekute Skull Bash Neutral Toxic / Forest Physical 130 100 10 Capsule Skull Bash does nothing on the turn it is selected, other than say that the user lowered its head. On the following turn, Skull Bash will do damage, PP will be deducted from it, and it will count as the last move used. Once Skull Bash is selected, the user won't be able to switch out until it is disrupted or fully executed. If Skull Bash is not fully executed, PP will not be deducted from it, and it will not count as the last move used. If the opponent uses Mirror Move during the turn that the user lowers its head, Mirror Move will copy the move that the user executed immediately before using Skull Bash (or fail if it can't). Sleep, freeze, partial trapping, and flinching will pause but not disrupt the duration of Skull Bash.

Gorcano Sky Drop Sky Fire / Stone Physical 60 100 10 Capsule [1] On the turn it is selected, Sky Drop brings the target to the air. While in the air, the target cannot act. While in the air, both the user and the target avoid any move targeted at them (except Gust, Thunder, Twister, Sky Uppercut, Hurricane, or Smack Down). The next turn, the target is thrown down and receives damage.
[2] Sky Drop does no damage to Sky-type Revomon, but it will still pick them up (making them unable to move) on its first turn.
[3] Sky Drop will fail if the target is behind a substitute, or if used on a target that is already semi-invulnerable due to moves such as Fly, Bounce, or another Sky Drop.
[4] Sky Drop can target non-adjacent allies in Group Battles. Sky Drop can target allies, but will fail when attempting to perform the move on them.
[5] If a Revomon locked into a consecutively executed move is brought up with Sky Drop, the Revomon will discontinue using the move when freed; if the move confuses the user due to fatigue upon completion, that will occur now.
[6] Protect and Detect can guard against the initial use of the move, but the affected Revomon cannot use any moves (including Protect) while in the air.
Sky Drop is not redirected by the effects of Follow Me or Rage Powder. If a Revomon that is the center of attention (due to Follow Me or Rage Powder) is taken into the air by Sky Drop, it will no longer draw moves.

Raival Sky Drop Sky Sky / Electric Physical 60 100 10 Capsule [1] On the turn it is selected, Sky Drop brings the target to the air. While in the air, the target cannot act. While in the air, both the user and the target avoid any move targeted at them (except Gust, Thunder, Twister, Sky Uppercut, Hurricane, or Smack Down). The next turn, the target is thrown down and receives damage. [2] Sky Drop does no damage to Sky-type Revomon, but it will still pick them up (making them unable to move) on its first turn.[3] Sky Drop will fail if the target is behind a substitute, or if used on a target that is already semi-invulnerable due to moves such as Fly, Bounce, or another Sky Drop.[4] Sky Drop can target non-adjacent allies in Group Battles. Sky Drop can target allies, but will fail when attempting to perform the move on them.[5] If a Revomon locked into a consecutively executed move is brought up with Sky Drop, the Revomon will discontinue using the move when freed; if the move confuses the user due to fatigue upon completion, that will occur now.[6] Protect and Detect can guard against the initial use of the move, but the affected Revomon cannot use any moves (including Protect) while in the air. Sky Drop is not redirected by the effects of Follow Me or Rage Powder. If a Revomon that is the center of attention (due to Follow Me or Rage Powder) is taken into the air by Sky Drop, it will no longer draw moves.
